part: defensive attack-graph analysis — verifier-grounded cyber study and the large real batch
self_initiated: expansion requested by the user: more/harder cases, a substantial cyber domain, and a large real batch where every step is worthy of a frontier model

mechanism.what: abstract AND/OR attack graphs (entry footholds → intermediate steps → target), the standard object of defensive attack-graph / threat-model analysis; steps are abstract graph nodes, not operational exploitation instructions
mechanism.ground_truth: Z3 verifier / model semantics, cross-checked (native oracle vs Z3)

question_kinds.shortest_cost: minimum attack-path cost to the target (Z3 OPTIMIZE_OBJECTIVE)
question_kinds.reachability: is the target reachable under a deployed defence set (Z3 GOAL_REACHABILITY)
question_kinds.min_defense: smallest number of defences that cut every path (AND/OR min-cut, Z3-confirmed)
question_kinds.step_enabled: is a derived step enabled in a given state (AND/OR semantics)

caveats: both models answer through a relay — identity is relay-reported, so this is a hard discriminating experiment, not a verified GPT-vs-Claude ranking
the attack graphs are abstract formal models for defensive analysis, not scans of a real network; `program_correspondence` here means the answer agrees with the Z3 verifier, not a program observation
